rows.label: dromedary
rows.desc:
A large land mammal adapted to arid environments. Domesticated since ancient times, its leather is exceptionally good at insulating against the desert heat, and its milk is quite nourishing. It can be used as a pack animal and mount, but its bouncing gait makes it slower to ride than a horse.

By storing water in its large humps and reclaiming moisture from its breath as it exhales, it can go weeks without drinking.

When in a caravan, people can ride dromedaries to increase the caravan's speed.

rows.label: royal ave
rows.desc:
Royal Aves are large flightless birds with colourful feathers. Royal Aves were originally wild Meadow Aves that have been cross-bred for generations to reduce their stubbornness and increase their fluffiness. Some of these prized pets get freed into the wild, a life that they are poorly adapted for. Plumage in Royal Aves is more flamboyant than usual: if lucky you might get your hands on the incredibly rare Rainbow Ave, which does nothing special besides from looking bizarre.

Royal Aves are amazing mounts, much faster than horses, and if properly trained they can be ridden into battle at incredible speeds (this interaction needs the Giddy-Up, combat mounts mod, and it will make the Royal Aves move 50% faster when used as mounts).

rows.label: windbeast
rows.desc:
The windbeast is a mechanoid-infused variant of the thunderbeast, in which the bioelectric organs have been removed and replaced with fleshy tentacles housing a distributed net of weather-affecting mechanites.

These deployable mechanite swarms have the ability to affect the weather in a localized manner, creating pressure gradients that may evolve into full-blown hurricane winds. This effect is used offensively by the creature, and is specially dangerous if it is killed, as the large sudden release of all mechanites can cause a tornado. Thankfully, predators usually give them a wide berth and they are quite rare.

rows.label: teratogenic originator
rows.desc:
This amorphous, flesh coloured, translucent creature seems to lack everything but the most basic instincts, moving around slowly and sometimes devouring any plant it comes in contact with, incorporating it into its cytoplasm. There are some chunks of seemingly normal flesh floating inside it.

Teratogenic Originators are basically an enormous clonal colony of pluripotent stem cells, capable of differentiating into different tissues. They were engineered by a group of unethical scientists as a cheap way to create lab-grown limbs suitable for transplants, but the end results is less than ideal. These strange mutant limbs can be periodically excised from the creature and used at will. Note that asexual creatures can't be sterilized.

rows.label: frostbound behemoth
rows.desc:
This large arthropod seems to be a distant relative of the smaller Frostmite, sharing many similarities in its body plan, though none of their carrion eating habits. It is a creature adapted to extreme low temperatures, feeding on half inorganic vegetation present in the unnatural propane lakes. Its slow metabolism makes it a very efficient creature, which allows it to survive in such environments.

It is generally peaceful, and produces a blueish liquid that can be used as a milk substitute, so they are considered a nice farm animal for cold climates. Also, Jedi love this milk.

An elusive and deceitful creature, the red-horned larpah is a large leporidae with tall brown antlers protruding from it's head. While it may look gentle, larpah's apperence belies its predatory, fierce nature. As they grow older, a thick layer of dried blood from past battles coats their horns, earning them the moniker of "red-horned".

Deadly and tough for its size, its aggressiveness rarely discourages hunters from trying their luck at slaying the beast for its durable pelt and valuable antlers, which can be turned into a powerful mixture.

rows.label: drainer larva
rows.desc:
A mostly harmless, cat-sized lepidopteran with brightly coloured wings. Drainers were originally blue morpho butterflies that mutated due to exposure to high levels of radiation in some wretched planet of the Rim. Though they can feed on grass if there is no other food available, they are actually electrovores, feeding on any available source of electricity. Unfortunately for colonies on the Rim, this means batteries...

Drainers undergo metamorphosis like most other lepidopterans, though their larval stage is pretty short, and doesn't have the energy draining abilities of the adults.

Art by Feroxiious (check her Instagram at https://www.instagram.com/feroxiious/).

rows.label: aerofleet
rows.desc:
A small, floating gelatinous creature. Propelled by the hydrogen it collects from water and various plant matter, these squishy creatures wander the lands, aimlessly bouncing off objects in their path. One of the few rare creatures around here that strangely isn’t out for human blood. Well, isn’t that nice?

Aerofleets are genderless, and reproduce by strobilation, a form of asexual reproduction. Note that asexual creatures can't be sterilized. As a floating creature, Aerofleets ignore terrain movement costs.

Aerofleets slowly produce a thick, gelatinous substance known as Blue Gel. This syrupy residue can be collected and refined into an energy-dense compound, and potentially used to build powerful batteries and generators, with the appropriate research (Biofuel refining, Batteries and Advanced Fabrication).

Art by Feroxiious (check her Instagram at https://www.instagram.com/feroxiious/).

rows.desc:
A large genetically engineered pill-bug. These creatures once served as the frontline skirmishers of an insectoid hive; A collection of genetically modified insects made as a weapon against Mechanoid invasions. The dwarven muffton is sheep-like herbivore known for its warm brown wool and gigantic horns. Herds can be often seen hopping around in the cold northern mountains where they live most of the year. rows.label: groundrunner
rows.desc:
A strange chimera between a bear and mole, Groundrunners originally came from Cave Worlds. They were used as walking heavy tools by the locals when they hit parts that plasteel can’t break, and for hauling large boulders that their owners can’t lift.

Due to their domesticated origins, they are surprisingly docile and easy to tame. Their incredible strength and sharp claws allows them to break rocks with relative ease. But out here in the Rim, those claws are usually reserved for ripping power armors apart along with their wearers.

Groundrunners will happily help your colonists mine rocks and minerals. They are however quite lazy and get distracted easily (this interaction requires the Groundrunner to be trained in Haul). This interaction should also work with the Quarry mod.

This large, genetically-engineered insectoid is part of the Black Hive, an artificial ecosystem of insectoids designed to fight mechanoid invasions. rows.label: mature fleshbeast
rows.desc:
The unwanted result of a genetic experiment gone wrong, fleshbeasts are usually miserable, weak creatures that ooze pus and struggle to keep breathing for longer than a few days. Sometimes, however, a fleshbeast manages to survive, and even thrive. Perhaps it was foolishly released into the wild, where it managed to stabilize and grow. Or perhaps it was stronger than average, and managed to subdue and devour its imprudent creators. In any case, it has now turned into a pulsating, fleshy behemoth with a ravenous appetite.

Mature fleshbeasts swallow their prey whole, storing up to 5 creatures on its huge stomach for later consumption. Prey may survive for up to one day, but they'll later be consumed and expelled as skeletized remains.

rows.label: angel moth larva
rows.desc:
Angel moths are beautiful lepidopterans that undergo metamorphosis, similar to other more mundane moths. Angel moths are yet another example of a genetically engineered project of waste disposal being abandoned, and its subjects being released into the wild.

The larvae are quite timid and harmless, and they are content with munching on sparse vegetation. The adult form of the moth, however, is voracious, and it will mainly consume its favourite food: clothing –in particular wool clothes, but many other natural fibres–. If no clothes are present they'll grudgingly devour grass. Although they can be used to get rid of unwanted clothing, it is hard to make them discriminate, as they are quite unruly creatures.

Adult specimens produce a moth silk that can be harvested to use as a textile, though care must be taken to keep it out of other moths' reach, since they'll happily consume it too.

rows.label: larval atispec
rows.desc:
Atispecs are strange semi-insectoid creatures that undergo a radical metamorphosis, similar to old terran butterflies. In their larval phase, atispecs are basically harmless: a medium-sized grub that feeds on plants and usually ends up as some predator's meal. Tens of thousands of atispec larvae hatch every season, and less than a dozen make it to their adult form.

An adult Atispec, however, is an entirely different matter: huge, carnivorous and venomous. Adult Atispecs are flying predators with a voracious appetite, and quite intelligent. There have been attempts to domesticate the adult specimens, but it has been found that it is not quite cost-effective to grow them during their 2-year-long vulnerable phase as larvae.

rows.label: shock goat
rows.desc:
Shock goats are domesticated cattle, renowned for their capacity to store static electricity on their bony structures, and releasing it as a defensive measure. Interestingly enough, the shock goat has characteristics common to many other Rim species, such as three pairs of eyes, and characteristics typical of Earth goats, such as the horns. This points to the conclusion that shock goats are actually a fertile cross-bred of two different creatures, created in the past by some human colony, and released in the wild for unknown reason.

Whatever the mystery behind their origins, nowadays they are commonly seen in farming communities in several Rim worlds, because they produce decent amounts of milk.

rows.label: razorjack
rows.desc:
The Razorjack is a very aggressive and adaptable creature with a strange body plan: a dual-jawed mouth that leads to two separate but intertwined digestive systems, each of them adapted to consume different types of food. This arrangement makes them extremely energy-efficient, and require very little food. Although it might seem canine at first, its genome has more in common with rodents, with some unusual genetic splicing thrown into the mix. Wounds caused by Razorjacks tend to get infected very easily.

Razorjacks can live in the most desolate conditions, since their need for food is very low. The most ferocious Razorjacks are specially trained, bred and further mutated into fearsome warbeasts, known as Razortooth, used by Feral warlords as terrifying warhounds. (Original concept for the Razortooth by Rooki12k, in the Rimsenal: Feral mod)

The pair of fleshy tentacles extending from a ray-hound's skull are electrogenic, and are used by the animal as a defense mechanism against predators. In practice, Ray-hounds were created as an easily trainable biological defense against mechanoids, since an electrical discharge from a ray-hound's tentacles can easily disable electronic circuits. A truly giant amphibian, this fearsome creature has hind legs that are mounds of pure muscle, allowing it to race horses and come out on top. Their skin is hard, leathery and bumpy, marked by islets of darker coulouration. Their enormous throat sacs let them call mates and make threats that can be heard over many miles. Their tongues shoot out at bullet speed when pursuing prey, be it large flies or small animals, able to penetrate armour and deal serious injury. Their leather is as thick as a bears, whom they sometimes fight for ownership of damp caves. Their meat tastes so much like chicken that you really can't feel the difference at all!  Not originally from this RimWorld, giant toads are the result of genetic engineering targeted at teraforming planets to rich agricultural swamps. How it got here is anyone's guess.

rows.label: giant snaptoad
rows.desc:
An enormous, carnivorous amphibian reigning as swamplands' apex predator. The tooth-filled maw that earned giant snaptoad its moniker can easily crush bone, and unhinge to swallow smaller prey whole after a leaping ambush from between the reeds. Its dentition, unique among contemporary amphibians, leads to speculation among scholars about whether giant snaptoad is a true toad, or an unrelated amphibian that convergently developed toad-like traits.

Giant snaptoads practice a rare form of child rearing called gastric brooding: upon fertilization, the eggs are immediately swallowed by the female and stored in a special chamber in their stomach. There, the tadpoles can safely hatch and develop, regurgitated by their parent only once they have transformed into froglets. However, in rare cases, the practice is omitted, and the tadpoles are left to fend for themselves in marshy waters.

rows.label: infected aerofleet
rows.desc:
A small, floating gelatinous creature. Propelled by the hydrogen it collects from water and various plant matter, these squishy creatures wander the lands, aimlessly bouncing off objects in their path.

This Aerofleet seems to have been affected by prolonged exposure to the gases emanating from an ocular forest, and red pustules and blisters are appearing in its exterior membrane. Its hydrogen seems to be in the process of being turned into an acidic gas of unknown origins.

Aerofleets are genderless, and reproduce by strobilation, a form of asexual reproduction. Note that asexual creatures can't be sterilized. As a floating creature, Aerofleets ignore terrain movement costs.

Aerofleets slowly produce a thick, gelatinous substance known as Blue Gel. This syrupy residue can be collected and refined into an energy-dense compound, and potentially used to build powerful batteries and generators with the appropriate research (Biofuel refining, Batteries and Advanced Fabrication).

A mostly harmless, cat-sized lepidopteran with brightly coloured wings. Drainers were originally blue morpho butterflies that mutated due to exposure to high levels of radiation in some wretched planet of the Rim. Though they can feed on grass if there is no other food available, they are actually electrovores, feeding on any available source of electricity. Unfortunately for colonies on the Rim, this means batteries...

Drainers undergo metamorphosis like most other lepidopterans, though their larval stage is pretty short, and doesn't have the energy draining abilities of the adults.

rows.label: ocular jelly
rows.desc:
The Rim is filled with creatures that might be the product of either accelerated evolution from terrestrial origins, or, more often, of ancient human genetic engineering gone awry. The ocular jelly, however, is so fundamentally weird that some scientists have speculated about a possible extradimensional origin. Or perhaps it is just some cruel, if elaborate, practical joke.

It seems to have some biological similarities with the Aerofleet, being filled with a buoyant gas, but its effects on terrestrial ecosystems are incredibly unusual: the creature releases clouds of a reddish gas that is harmless to animals. However, when flora is exposed to it, it mutates and turns into strange specimens that share 98% of its genome with the jelly. This flora is almost inedible, and its relationship with the ocular jelly remains as of yet unexplained. As a floating creature, Ocular Jellies ignore terrain movement costs. Note that asexual creatures can't be sterilized.

rows.desc:
The Helixien Slug is a genetically modified strain of the Leopard Slug, intended as a fast corpse disposal aid. Aside from the obvious size alteration, the Helixien constantly secretes a foul-smelling, corrosive gas that produces an uncomfortable, itchy sensation in living beings. This gas is mostly harmless, unless it comes into contact with decaying organic matter: it greatly accelerates corpse rotting, liberating a black putrid liquid known as "purge fluid" or corpse bile. The helixien happily feeds on this liquid sludge, although it can also feed on other organic matter if needed.

The sight of a Helixien Slug is quite revolting, and watching one wallowing in a pile of human corpses is, to say the least, a deeply traumatizing experience.

The war wyrm was originally an infant exogorth that had been mutated and warped by Sith alchemy. They were very rare and very large and several specimens were believed to have been left behind by Sith armies on various worlds having fulfilled their roles as apex siege beasts.

A eusocial creature, it cannot reproduce individually.

rows.label: crescendo anole
rows.desc:
Most of the time, the Crescendo Anole is a harmless iguanian lizard that feeds on vegetation and small arthropods. They are unusually intelligent, and can be kept as pets. However, when the anole becomes aggressive in any way, usually in self defense, an unstable cocktail of growth hormones and biomechanical mechanites causes a runaway growth of the creature's cells, turning it into a hulking crocodilian nightmare.

This effect is temporary, lasting a few hours, and afterwards the anole must recover its strength to be able to go through it again, becoming extremely hungry in the interim.

rows.label: metallovore
rows.desc:
Metallovores are repulsive creatures genetically modified to fill a very specific niche: eating metals. The writhing tentacles in the animal's mouth secrete an organic substance that is capable of quickly rusting and dissolving most common metals, turning them into small flakes that serve as sustenance for the metallovore. They prefer small chunks of metal, since they can be more easily digested, but they will resort to digging into rocks in search of new metal if they can find none available.

Presumably, they were created to get rid of scrap metal, but they are mostly found in the wild now.

Lava fleas were also very suitable mounts and exported as such to worlds with inhospital climates to other creatures.

rows.label: murkling
rows.desc:
A distant relative of the nightling, murklings are -in fact- quite their opposite. They are not as fierce nor are they proficient hunters, often scavenging in packs for scraps left behind by the more apt predators.  Their most distinctive features are the abnormally elongated structures on their snouts, which are theorized to produce specific vibrational sequences that allow for discrete communication between pack members. Their physical weakness is compensated for with above average intellect, allowing them to outsmart organisms as intelligent as the Forsaken. Their reputation for stealthily stealing supplies across the Rim has earned them the nickname 'thief of the night'.

Special abilities: A Murkling's bite can inflict the bubonic plague. The delicate tendrils on their snouts can dissolve nearby corpses and turn them into semi-liquid carrion that can feed the Murkling.

Night Aves have adapted to environments with very low sunlight, and they are purely nocturnal animals.

Night Aves are amazing mounts, much faster than horses, and if properly trained they can be ridden into battle at incredible speeds (this interaction needs the Giddy-Up, combat mounts mod, and it will make the Night Aves move 50% faster when used as mounts).

rows.desc: A result of failed animal weaponization trials, the dusk prowler is an ideal killing machine, built and modified to satisfy the requirements of fast-paced warfare. The fierce nature of the prowler is reinforced further by the muscular protrusions on their back, which simultaneously act as both accelerators and as weapons. Their capability to overrun even the most well defended military facilities resulted in the systematic purge that was commissioned by the intergalactic federations centuries ago, in hopes of driving the prowlers to extinction. Thus, very few prowler sightings are reported across the Rim nowadays, with those who see one almost never making it out alive to tell the tale.

rows.label: nightram
rows.desc:
The Nightram is a stubborn herbivore that shares much of its genome with the predatory Nightling, hinting at a common origin. They both originate from a RimWorld orbiting a very faint star -the native planet of an elusive race known as the Forsaken- so they have adapted to environments with low sunlight. When found on other worlds, the Nightram are exclusively nocturnal, instinctively avoiding natural sunlight.

Nightrams are peaceful unless disturbed or threatened.

rows.label: shadow charger
rows.desc:
A creature known for its mighty elongated horns, the Shadow Charger is actually rather passive, their horns only being used upon provocation or during mating. Their name is derived from their aggression against potential rivals during mating season, where the females are seen charging and locking horns with each other to secure a mate. While they were once used as battle mounts due to their speed and ability to ram, nowadays they are mostly raised across the Rim for their creamy milk and abundant meat.

Special abilities: Shadow chargers provide very good amounts of milk, and they can defend themselves much better than cows.

rows.label: nightmule
rows.desc:
The Nightmule is a hardy pack beast, used for transporting loads or doing other heavy work. Nightmules originate from a RimWorld orbiting a very faint star -the native planet of an elusive race know as the Forsaken- so they have adapted to environments with low sunlight. They were domesticated by the Forsaken hundreds of years ago, and can be found roaming around some other planets in the Rim.

Nightmules are stronger than muffalos, though they produce a very low amount of milk, and no wool. Similar to the Nightling, another creature from the Forsaken's planet, their back is crowned by dangerous quills, though the Nightmule lacks the capacity to throw them as defensive weapons.

It has been alternatively postulated that they came from that planet originally, spreading along with the Infinite Empire. Their exponential population growth led to them being considered pests on almost as many worlds as they inhabited, as they commonly ate electrical wiring. They were the source for the delicacy gizka steak.

They used their long, prehensile tongue to catch smaller prey, such as gorgs, but were known to also attack creatures larger than itself.

rows.label: needlepost
rows.desc:
A cactus genetically modified to give it sentience. The first iteration of this creature was supposed to be a stationary tactical deterrent (the Whip Cactus), but having no intelligence or mobility crippled its effectiveness. With a little genetic engineering, it was given a mobile body, an infantile intelligence, and toxic barbs for good measure. The result backfired as commands proved ineffective. The facility was promptly overrun by the experiments; and a horde of angry cacti escaped into the wilderness.

Needleposts can derive nutrition from very small amounts of rotting vegetables, but they need a huge amount of sunlight (or equivalent) over anything else. Nights won't affect them, but a solar eclipse is usually fatal to them.

It trails the fire fronts the way other things trail water, taking whatever the smoke pushes out of cover, and its serrated forelimb blades leave a wound that ash gets into and keeps.

When they hatched from their eggs, young hawk-bats had scaly green skin and were precocial, meaning they were fully independent and able to hunt upon the day of hatching. Upon reaching maturity, the hawk-bat would shed its green skin and emerge with mature purplish-gray skin.

rows.label: decay drake
rows.desc:
Decay Drakes are large, winged flightless lizards that inhabit places with an abundance of vegetation. Decay Drakes release a nauseous cocktail of volatile pheromones that quickly accelerates the rotting process of plants, turning vegetation around them into mounds of fermented organic matter. They will consume these and usually get incredibly drunk in the process. Interestingly, the creature has four separate livers in order to process the huge amounts of alcohol.

They aren't easy to domesticate, but if they can be coerced to accept humans, they might be useful hunting companions, specially if provided with alcohol...

Human beings have been known to consume the rotting vegetation in desperate times, but most people would rather starve.

Raptor shrimps have impressive regenerative capabilities, and shouldn't be considered dead until they absolutely, unmistakably, are.

The Thermadon is a large Blackspider that has been biologically augmented with volatile chemical glands. Originally, the Thermadon was bred by the long forgotten creators of the Black Hive as a fearsome fire-breathing shock trooper, using thermal grenades capable of affecting even fire-resistant Mechanoids, the primary objective of the Black Hive. Mechanoids however managed to adapt to these biological grenades quickly, and thus the Thermadon project was scrapped.

Apparently, some of them managed to escape into the wild.

Just... don't attack this thing if your base is made of wood, mmkay?

Project Apricus was a classified scientific endeavour on one of the RimWorlds aiming to discover new ways to fight the Mechanoid menace using nature. The mantrap was created as an attempt to weaponize a mutated Dionaea muscipula (Venus flytrap) by implanting concentrated formic acid spit launchers on its jaws. This strong acid was theoretically powerful enough to corrode the plasteel on Mechanoid carapaces.

Project Apricus was invaded by a huge Mechanoid host shortly thereafter, most of its personnel slain, and most of the projects left to fend for themselves.

rows.desc:
Although rare, mechanoids have been known to capture prisoners, and the Slurrypede is their solution to feed them in the most efficient way possible. The Slurrypede is a modified bio-mechanoid capable of devouring almost anything and processing it into a homogeneous organic slurry. This slurry is edible for carnivore and omnivore animals, but barely, and completely indigestible for herbivores.

Slurrypedes are docile, almost never hostile, and in case a mechanoid base is destroyed and one of them manages to survive, they tend to roam the wilderness aimlessly, consuming any organic material in their path and turning it into nutrient paste.

rows.label: tetra slug
rows.desc:
These massive slugs are a common sight among Glitterworld controlled territories, where they lumber about as glorified power plants. Outside of one, they are deployed as a mobile power source for Glitterworld research expeditions. It is rare to see one without the iconic power cores that protrude from their backs, as their unique bodily chemical composition is capable of outputting power that far surpasses any known natural sources. Thus, they are widely valued by every technologically developing civilization throughout the galaxy.

While a gentle giant that would prefer to run away instead of fight, modified slugs come armoured with plasteel shells, quad cores that can act as Tesla cannons, and a Tactical AI inserted within the brain that takes over and makes no hesitation to use all of its armament to obliterate any perceived threat within vicinity.

Properly outfitted Tetra slugs will slowly recharge batteries on their vicinity (most modded batteries are supported).

A wispy-looking creature that is the only known example of plasma-based life in the Rim: the Aurora Sylph is of artificial origins, and its biology is so strange that only the most advanced glitterworld technology could have been responsible for its creation. It is believed that the sylphs were created as a lifeform capable of surviving in the atmosphere of Red Dwarf stars, for utterly inscrutable purposes. They don't seem to be affected by gravity much, so they can also be found stranded in the gravity well of a planet.

Sylphs are immune to temperature extremes, though very fragile and easy to damage. They don't need to eat, as they will replenish their energy simply by absorbing light. If they are content, they will periodically influence the magnetic fields of a planet, and cause beautiful auroras, hence their name.

rows.desc: A migratory megafauna whose banded mineral hide stores heat like a stove — a slow thermal capacitor on legs. It charges in the Deep Desert, basking for weeks, then walks into the Pyrelands on purpose when the grass burns: it helps the fire along and drinks the heat of it, glowing brighter at the seams between its plates. Fully charged, a herd marches all the way out to the near terminator and eats everything in sight — it is one of the only things that will strip a thornvine patch — bleeding its banked warmth into the cold air for weeks before turning back to charge again. rows.label: angel moth
rows.desc:
Angel moths are beautiful lepidopterans that undergo metamorphosis, similar to other more mundane moths. Angel moths are yet another example of a genetically engineered project of waste disposal being abandoned, and its subjects being released into the wild.

The larvae are quite timid and harmless, and they are content with munching on sparse vegetation. The adult form of the moth, however, is voracious, and it will mainly consume its favourite food: clothing –in particular wool clothes, but many other natural fibres–. If no clothes are present they'll grudgingly devour grass. Although they can be used to get rid of unwanted clothing, it is hard to make them discriminate, as they are quite unruly creatures.

Adult specimens produce a moth silk that can be harvested to use as a textile, though care must be taken to keep it out of other moths' reach, since they'll happily consume it too.

They have been nicknamed green goo due to their ability to reproduce constantly, requiring very little sustenance, and quickly filling all available ecological niches. In the field of eschatology, a grey goo is an end-of-the-world scenario involving molecular nanotechnology in which out-of-control self-replicating robots consume all biomass while building more of themselves. A green goo scenario, however, involves biological self-replicating entities. NOTE: due to gameplay constraints, green goo will only self-replicate until the map holds 40 creatures, because I don't want to fry your computers. Note that asexual creatures can't be sterilized.

rows.label: mime
rows.desc:
Whereas most of the "alien" animals of the Rim are heavily genetically modified versions of Earth animals, the Mime is an absolute violation of all ethical principles: a ravenous, animalistic being created by genetically modifying humans.

Mimes are psionically gifted parasites, using their mental powers to disguise themselves as normal humans, infiltrating a human community and living among its members for weeks, months or even years. Their voracious appetites, however, cause them to constantly consume the easily available food provided by a stable colony. Only when food runs out will they resort to directly attacking their unwitting hosts.

rows.label: plasmorph
rows.desc:
This bizarre, mutant snail has a very strange way of defending itself against predators. Inside its armoured shell made of iron sulphide, specialized organs along the Plasmorph's body generate an electric discharge similar to those found in electric eels. This discharge is very low voltage, not powerful enough to damage most creatures. However, the Plasmorph uses it as a spark to ignite its own flammable spit, and lob it at its prey.

Such a strange mechanism is surely not natural, but what was its intended purpose is a mystery lost to the ages.

The Bumbledrone is a mutant wasp-like creature, probably the result of ancient genetic engineering long ago released into the wild. On its own, a Bumbledrone isn't very powerful, more a nuisance than a threat, but if threatened in big numbers their stingers carry a very powerful toxin that could down even the biggest foe. "Luckily", since they are not carnivorous, they use this as a deterrent, rather than as a hunting method. As a floating creature, Bumbledrones ignore terrain movement costs.

rows.label: fission mouse
rows.desc:
Even though this creature is usually called a mouse, it has more traits in common with the banner-tailed kangaroo rat, such as a jumping bipedal locomotion.

The fission mouse is yet another example of human genetic engineering gone terribly wrong. Presumably, the objective was to make the mice more useful as laboratory animals by increasing their resistance and longevity. The unexpected result is a sterile creature with neither attribute, but a really strange side effect: when the animal dies, three duplicates are created, sharing all memories of its parent.

Rapid successive fission events are also harmful to the creature itself. If less than a few years pass between events, the mouse eventually perishes, unable to sustain its life cycle.

Though it is easily tamed, the Megatardi is not without its dangers. Upon its death, it releases a cloud of toxic gas, making it a potential hazard for anyone nearby. Despite this, the Megatardi remains a valuable asset for those willing to take on the challenges of the polluted wasteland.

The Overgrown Colossus is a very strange beast. This gargantuan beast is one of the few creatures in the Rim that wasn't directly created by man's scientific curiosity, arising naturally in some remote swamp-filled planet, albeit from some original forgotten terran creature.

It seems to be reptilian in nature, with cold blood, a slow metabolism, and a very weird body plan: it has six legs, two intertwined spines and six eyes. It has a symbiotic relationship with vegetation, with several small trees growing on its back. These trees do photosynthesis and help provide nutrients for the Colossus.

When tamed, the Overgrown Colossus can be periodically "trimmed" to obtain wood.

Based on concept art by Arvalis: https://www.deviantart.com/arvalis/art/Overgrown-Colossus-Concept-Art-144699628

Just the sweetest little kitty cat you’ll ever encounter, they were bred as tiny caretakers to look after people in hospital wards. Despite being a health violation, they were extremely popular with the infirms as they not only fed patients but also engaged in conversation and gave friendly headbutts. It is also alleged that their purring helped broken bones heal quicker, but no conclusive evidence has been shown.

This increases the social recreation needs of those they interact with by 10% (subject to diminishing returns like all joy types). If using Ideology, humanoid hybrids are subject to precepts. Catmen are compassionate animals that will help with feeding medical patients around the colony.

rows.label: fission mouse, second generation
rows.desc:
Even though this creature is usually called a mouse, it has more traits in common with the banner-tailed kangaroo rat, such as a jumping bipedal locomotion.

The fission mouse is yet another example of human genetic engineering gone terribly wrong. Presumably, the objective was to make the mice more useful as laboratory animals by increasing their resistance and longevity. The unexpected result is a sterile creature with neither attribute, but a really unexpected side effect: when the animal dies, three duplicates are created, sharing all memories of its parent.

Rapid successive fission events are also harmful to the creature itself. If less than a few years pass between events, the mouse eventually perishes, unable to sustain its life cycle.

This fission mouse is of second generation, indicating the fission process has happened once recently, making it weaker.

Art by Feroxiious (check her Instagram at https://www.instagram.com/feroxiious/).

rows.desc:
The Bumbledrone is a mutant wasp-like creature, probably the result of ancient genetic engineering long ago released into the wild. On its own, a Bumbledrone isn't very powerful, more a nuisance than a threat, but if threatened in big numbers their stingers carry a very powerful toxin that could down even the biggest foe. "Luckily", since they are not carnivorous, they use this as a deterrent, rather than as a hunting method.

This particular bumbledrone seems to be a "queen", so called because it seems to deposit eggs from which other bumbledrones may hatch. It tends to do this specially once it has settled into an environment it considers safe, so it might be a really useful asset to tame it.

The danger comes from their eggs, whether fertilized or not: they constantly produce an intense heat, that might even cause fires in the vicinity. A single fire wasp egg unthinkingly placed in a refrigerator will be enough to spoil all the food inside.

It is territorial, and lives mainly alone or in pairs.

Contrary to other purely photosynthetic creatures, the caracal can also hunt small prey, and it needs both kinds of sustenance to survive.

A wonderful animal for those cold winter journeys, very popular as travellers snuggle into their fur at night to keep warm. Fights have even broken out over who gets to sleep with the oversized rug.

An ursine hybrid with recessive muffalo genes. Very filthy but a decently intelligent pack animal that produces good-quality wool and milk. Performs very well in cold environments and is more than capable of defending itself.

rows.desc:
For lovers of xenomorphs everywhere, this bomb-ass bombadier is ready to launch sacs of acidic chemfuel at your enemies for fun and profit. Don’t expect a second pair of jaws though, that mouth is for spitting only.

An insectoid hybrid with recessive boomalope genes. Quite temperamental for a hybrid, but they prove to be worth it as they store caustic chemfuel in their sacs which can then be lobbed at a distance. Practically useless in melee, so keep them safe and provide fire support. Can be ordered to detonate auxiliary acid sacs as a defensive measure, but that will also self-harm.

Combining the frequent nuzzling of a cat and the deepchem production of a primary boomalope hybrid is surely in no way going to end badly. Better not to ignore them should they complain loudly about wanting dinner.

A boomalope hybrid with recessive feline genes. They make for an interesting companion for those who desire chemfuel production but also want to be able to cuddle said creatures. They can also be butchered to retrieve an internal gland filled with deepchem.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> Like all cat hybrids, they have an improved melee dodge ability and a short nuzzle period.

rows.label: boomsnake
rows.desc:
What happens when you mix a spitting cobra, a rattlesnake and a creature designed to lactate refined fuel? This abomination, that’s what. Drive it into a corner and it’ll hurt itself to release deadly neurotoxins. Try and keep your distance and it’ll spit toxic blood right at you. Clearly someone was a sore loser in playing pretend games as a child, but had either the brains or the money to prove themselves right.

A reptile hybrid with recessive boomalope genes. Decently intelligent with a nasty bite and even nastier ranged attack, both causing toxic buildup. Quite a high metabolism which supports its various combat abilities, best suited for home defence.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> All reptile hybrids have good temperature tolerance ranges and venomous attacks.

rows.desc:
For those who wished they could equip their canines with explosive vests, the Boomwolf stores pressurised - almost solidified - chemfuel which can be remotely discharged as a non-explosive gas. Thanks to thermodynamics, it is extremely cold upon release and can just as easily hurt the hybrid as well as everything nearby.

A boomalope hybrid with recessive canine genes. Very intelligent, fast and dangerous, they make for an interesting combat animal. One of the few canine-type hybrids that work better solo than as a pack.

rows.label: lizardman
rows.desc:
It is doubtful that one would meet a crueller or more sadistic creature than this hybrid. It actively experiences joy when slaughtering tame animals and executing prisoners, the latter of which even provides a powerful boost which can be used before battle. Maybe it has something to do with taking pleasure in killing those that made it this way, but that’s a story for another time.

A reptile hybrid with recessive humanoid genes. A very intelligent but combat-limited animal that performs surprisingly poorly against similar sized creatures. They will only passively engage creatures much smaller than itself and takes some twisted, psychotic pleasure in killing those who are completely helpless.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> Humanoid hybrids will periodically engage other colonists in conversation, talking about a variety of topics. This increases the social recreation needs of those they interact with by 10% (subject to diminishing returns like all joy types). If using Ideology, humanoid hybrids are subject to precepts. All reptile hybrids have good temperature tolerance ranges and venomous attacks. Lizardmen will obey order to slaughter other colony animals, as well as execute prisoners of the colony.

rows.desc:
A creature originally designed for other recreational purposes before that particular laboratory of degenerates got glassed from orbit, they make for an affectionate conversation partner. You know, probably, most likely, until their particular speech pattern grinds on your nerves like a cheese grater.

A humanoid hybrid with recessive feline genes. A surprisingly large yet timid predator that can output a disturbing amount of damage. Typically fun to talk to, but 10% of the time it tries to be a little too cute.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> Like all cat hybrids, they have an improved melee dodge ability and a short nuzzle period. In the case of the mancat, these interactions will 90% of the time increase the targets' social joy by 15%, but the rest of the time they'll just make the target very annoyed... Useful abilities: if properly trained they can be ridden into battle at incredible speeds (this interaction needs the Giddy-Up, combat mounts mod, and it will make the Meadow Lizards move 100% faster when used as mounts). They are also venomous.

rows.desc:
This cybernetic boomalope has been outfitted with four mechanized chemfuel reservoirs. The creature can use these reservoirs to produce a jet of burning fuel similar to a flamethrower, not incredibly harmful, but perfect for starting huge fires.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> Mechanoid hybrids are always created with a controller booster, making the mechalope an effective weapons platform, akin to a flamethrower. Mechanoid hybrids need very little food or rest, don't have psychic or toxic sensitivity, and have devastating ranged attacks. They have however high wildness, making them harder to keep tamed, and they will need a mechahybrid antenna to be built somewhere on the planet, or their IFF sensors will malfunction in 5 days. One antenna is needed for each five mech hybrids under the colony's control.

rows.desc:
A hulking monstrosity that is genuinely caring for those around them, taking great joy and actual personal pleasure through working diligently and caring for those it considers friends and family. Evidently, it was bred specifically by megacorporations to work in dangerous mines, because human greed never changes.

A rodent hybrid with recessive humanoid genes. Very low hunger rate and very intelligent, these gentle giants enjoy digging with their hands. They will sometimes work mining orders given the chance but they’re very slow due to their bulk.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> Humanoid hybrids will periodically engage other colonists in conversation, talking about a variety of topics. This increases the social recreation needs of those they interact with by 10% (subject to diminishing returns like all joy types). If using Ideology, humanoid hybrids are subject to precepts. rows.label: muffaloman
rows.desc:
The animal we’ve all been waiting for, namely one that not only cleans up after itself but for others as well. Their fur is surprisingly soft and has antibacterial properties, which it uses along with its fingered paws to clean surfaces. Once the fur starts to become matted is when it needs to be trimmed.

A muffalo hybrid with recessive humanoid genes. Quite intelligent but they lose out on a lot of their progenitor’s hardiness against the cold. They are also very clean animals and will clean areas around the colony, and can be sheared regularly for a decent amount of wool.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> Humanoid hybrids will periodically engage other colonists in conversation, talking about a variety of topics. This increases the social recreation needs of those they interact with by 10% (subject to diminishing returns like all joy types). If using Ideology, humanoid hybrids are subject to precepts. All primary muffalo hybrids have 150% carrying capacity on caravans. Muffalomen are clean muffalo hybrids that will periodically clean around the colony.

rows.label: muffalopede
rows.desc:
An oversized grub with udders that extrude jelly instead of milk, its hard-headedness serves it well in both getting what it wants and nutting anyone foolish enough to think they’re better than them. Allegedly there was a case where the owner was prevented from shearing the creature for so long that the overlapping plates completely prevented it from moving, who was afterwards thanked with a kick in the nether region.

An insectoid hybrid with recessive muffalo genes. Higher metabolism compared to other insectoid hybrids as well as stubborn, any predator foolish enough to think of them as an easy meal will be responded with a headbutt like a sledgehammer. Can work as a pack animal but refuses to haul comparatively heavy loads. Regularly produces precious jelly and can be sheared for chitin, which overlaps and protects the animal well from blunt attacks.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> All insectoid hybrids have good armor and no toxic sensitivity, but they are always sterile and can't reproduce, even if a fertility booster is used to create them.

rows.desc:
Possibly one of the weirdest and cutest snakes to be ever created. They have several tiny legs which are used to push its body along, while also having an invitingly soft fur. Quite a lot of people never stop freaking out from something sliding up the backs of their legs only to get softly headbutted by a purring python.

A reptile hybrid with recessive feline genes. An unusually furry snake that enjoys nuzzling while also hunting for prey much weaker than itself. Incredibly intelligent and easy to train, they combine quick reflexes and an incredibly nasty bite and spitting attack.

rows.desc:
Practically an overgrown and intelligent pest capable of tunnelling underground, so not even a nuke could clear an infestation. And it truly would be an infestation, as it has a gestation period measured in days rather than weeks, with a single breeding pair capable of wiping out an entire agricultural planet.

A colossal hybrid with recessive rodent genes. Incredibly durable and fast breeding, this surprisingly small hybrid can work as a durable screening force. One of the weakest colossal hybrids in terms of attack power but very few can outlast its incredibly robust physique.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> All colossal hybrids have very slow attacks, but hit very hard, and possess natural armor. Burrow underground: Thrumborats can burrow underground to make them almost immune to damage for a short while.

A canine hybrid with recessive muffalo genes. A great producer of thick wool and, regrettably, hairy milk. This allows them to survive in even more extreme colds, but they frequently make a mess, lack most of their intellect and need to eat a lot.

rows.desc:
A basic reusable transport pod, the Frog is a relatively cheap vehicle that is the first option when it comes to flying without crashing into the ground. Several times faster than conventional transport pods with acceptable armour for its single passenger, making it an ideal ambush vehicle.

Even worse than other tier 1 vehicles, fuel efficiency isn’t a thing with this transportation. Care must be taken to either refuel at the landing site or travel with enough spare fuel to make the trip back.

Being a flying vehicle, it is extremely obvious when on the move.

A squad and mortar deployment pod, the Toad is a somewhat expensive vehicle to quickly mount a siege on a nearby locale without exposing your gunners to danger. With more armour than a tank and a design made to be deployed from orbit, it makes for a semi-disposable assault vehicle.

Fuel efficiency is not the design of this vehicle, consider only deploying on short distances with enough fuel to make it back.

Being a flying vehicle, it is extremely obvious when on the move.

rows.label: Outrigger Canoe
rows.desc:
A watercraft featuring a lateral support float known as an outrigger, which is fastened to one of the sides of the main hull. An outrigger generates stability as a result of the distance between its hulls rather than due to the shape of each individual hull. As such, the hulls of outrigger boats are typically longer, narrower and more hydrodynamically efficient.

This cryo-weapon has a very low range, but it can be very dangerous for beings susceptible to frostbite.

A rodent hybrid with recessive muffalo genes. Quite clever, almost absurdly lethal and quick on its feet. While they are herbivores, they will still happily munch on corpses thanks to their large appetite. Not as short a gestation period compared to other primary rodent hybrids, but every bite transmits the plague.

A muffalo hybrid with recessive avian genes. A bit too slow and weak for a caravan companion but it makes  for a vicious and suicidal protective companion. Produces a thick, chunky milk that tastes like a protein shake.

A perfect feline animal, paragon of all similar animals with no needless junk genetic data. rows.label: frost lynx
rows.desc:
A genetically altered hybrid of a lynx and a snow leopard, the Frost lynx shares its genetic template with the Genix, both having diverged due to environmental pressure after their creation.

The Frost lynx was modified with hydrofluorocarbon-laced hemoglobin in its blood, allowing it to survive in extremely low temperatures, with a core body heat that would normally kill most creatures. As such, it is capable of using its low body heat to cause frostbite wounds in its victims, quickly incapacitating them. If it feels threatened, it can produce a ranged spit projectile containing particles of its blood, which explodes on impact and coves an area in dangerous freezing crystals.

A genetically altered hybrid of a lynx and a snow leopard, the Genix shares its genetic template with the Frost lynx, both having diverged due to environmental pressure after their creation.

Whereas the Frost lynx is perfectly adapted to cold temperatures, the Genix is usually found on milder climates, as it has a complex biological refrigeration system that allows it to decrease ambient temperature wherever it goes. If domesticated, this strange ability could perhaps be used to refrigerate an enclosed space. However, the Genix has a tendency to explode if it receives too much damage, making it a quite fragile creature.

One dewback, a yoke, and a light two-wheeled platform to stand on. It is the fastest thing a scavenger clan can build out of scrap, and it is fast only where the ground is already flat and packed.

Dewbacks are big grey-green lizards that do not hurry and do not need to. They drink at dawn, walk through the worst of the heat without complaint, and will keep a steady pace long after a warm-blooded animal has lain down in whatever shade it can find.

Off a road the chariot is close to useless — the wheels are narrow, they cut into soft sand, and the rider spends more time hauling it free than riding it.

rows.label: eopie sled
rows.desc:
Two eopies in harness, and a flatbed of lashed scrap riding on runners because wheels drown in soft sand.

They are patient, sour-smelling animals with long necks and a hide like cracked leather, and they will walk all day on almost nothing. Water they need. Food they mostly find, chewing whatever grey thing is rooted between the rocks. They complain constantly through their snouts, they spit when handled badly, and they are worth every bit of it — an eopie team will cross open pan in the heat of the day and be ready to do it again after a night's rest and a trough.

The sled is the point. Runners spread the load where a cart would dig in, so you can haul a wreck's worth of salvage back across the flats instead of picking through it for what fits in a pack.

rows.desc:
A small Arctic whale with a single spiralled tooth grown out through its lip, sometimes longer than the rest of its head. It spends the winter under pack ice, breathing at cracks, and goes down past fifteen hundred meters after squid - an hour at a time, in the dark, with the whole weight of the water on it.

It does none of the things a deep-sea animal does. Its body is an ordinary mammal's, warm and jointed, and it simply holds its breath and comes back up.

Like any whale it is a warm-blooded air breather doing this on one lungful, and it comes back up unchanged.

rows.desc:
Two rontos in front of a four-wheeled wagon with a hide roof stretched over hoops. The roof is not comfort. It is the difference between arriving and arriving with heatstroke.

Rontos are enormous, dun-coloured and profoundly nervous. They will carry a house across open pan all day and then bolt at a shadow, so the harness is built to come apart faster than it goes on, and nobody sensible sleeps under the wheels.

Leather strapping under the bed takes the worst of the ruts out. Three can ride in the back without arriving bruised, which on a two-day crossing is worth more than speed.

An absolute unit of an insectoid hybrid, this massive chubster is incredibly smart and hard to kill. All the excess blubber has been replaced with either chitin or muscle fibre, so don’t go making comments about their bulk.

An insectoid hybrid with recessive ursine genes. Very thick armour plating and a calm temperament make this hybrid an excellent combat animal. Requires little in the way of retraining and can dish out respectable damage as well.

rows.desc:

Useful abilities: Produces wool, milk, acts as a pack beast and  mines rocks and minerals.

rows.label: nighthrumbo
rows.desc:
The nighthrumbo is a fearsome predator. Armed with strong jaws and its horn, as well as ranged quill attacks, it will make quick work of any prey it decides to attack. It is also a nocturnal animal, sleeping during the day and being active at night.

Useful abilities: Ranged quill attacks.

rows.label: equine paragon
rows.desc:
The most majestic of horses is proud and magnificent, and doesn’t care for your rules, man. So keep them properly penned up, because they’ll try to escape to freedom so they can run wild and free. And then wonder where all the carrots, sugar cubes and salt licks have disappeared to.

A perfect equine animal, paragon of all similar animals with no needless junk genetic data. Besides the various improvements to the baseline animal’s abilities, this paragon makes for an excellent mount and pack animal for caravans.

specials.text: can carry cargo in a caravan

rows.diet: live plants, fungus, seeds, vegetables and fruit; will also take kibble and cooked food

rows.label: thrumbochicken
rows.desc:
This is probably the closest chickens will be able to get to recovering their past glory as super predators. They’ll often hunt any other animal for their next meal, multiple times a day, and you haven’t yet lived until you’ve ridden one on a long journey. If they could be further bred to cross mountains and oceans, they’d be almost perfect.

A colossal hybrid with recessive avian genes. The combination of genes has turned this somewhat peaceful herbivore/dendrovore into a full carnivore, which makes it easier to support their large appetite. As an intelligent predator, it can move incredibly quickly for its size and its attacks are incredibly fierce. It also lays massive eggs that can feed entire families.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> All colossal hybrids have very slow attacks, but hit very hard, and possess natural armor.

rows.label: muffalohorse
rows.desc:
Belligerent bulls with a penchant for the tastes of the wild wastes. A herd of these creatures can be occasionally seen trawling through regions, consuming practically all edible vegetation and leaving fertile waste in their path. Some argue that this is the ideal form of muffalo for nomad tribes, as they produce everything they need to survive winters and are large enough to feed said tribe through the harshest of seasons.

An equine hybrid with recessive muffalo genes. Very unusual in that it doesn’t help a caravan speed along, largely due to it excessively foraging and eating various vegetation from new locations, as well as roughage to help with digestion. The benefit from this behaviour is that this stimulation is the only way it’ll produce milk and wool, so herds of these hybrids can be taken on a long journey to provide produce vital to small and starting colonies.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> All equine hybrids are good for caravaning. A caravan with one of them needs a shorter resting period, only stopping to rest between 23:30 PM and 4 AM.

They are relatively slow and easy to kill, but once they die, they explode into a horde of smaller fleshbeasts.

While they’re surprisingly tireless when they have a home to rest at, these manned mares are quite reluctant to hurry along when made to carry loads in a caravan. Their body’s efficiency means they’ll get a task done when it needs to, and not a moment sooner. What makes it worse is that they’re smart enough to know that they’re cute - and powerful - enough to get away with it.

An equine hybrid with recessive ursine genes. The inherent hibernating nature of bears has combined with the high energy of horses to create this particular hybrid that requires little in the way of rest and a much more efficient and versatile digestive system. They are quite a bit slower as a consequence, along with their higher body mass.

Milking snakes for venom in order to create medicine is an extremely dangerous career. While this particular beast of burden proved to be capable in other areas, it was mainly synthesised in order to provide a safer way of sourcing an anaesthetic coagulant to be used in emergencies. Or someone was trying to get high by milking a reptilian space cow, who really knows.

A reptile hybrid with recessive muffalo genes. A strong pack animal with a massive appetite and a proportionate filth rate. Quite durable and will prove a fatal mistake for any animal that attempts to hunt them, as their fangs, horns and claws are all venomous. Can be milked every ten days for a vial of paralysing coagulant, best used for large animals that are suffering from multiple lacerations.

Known as a prime male, this massive insectoid is equipped with lethal ripper claws sharp enough to cleave armored vehicles in two. Complementing its fearsome offensive capabilities, the teramantis boasts a large set of wings, granting it the ability to soar across the vast landscapes in pursuit of prey for hundreds of miles. Its aerial prowess and deadly strength make it a dreaded apex predator on Chelis, commanding respect and fear from all who dwell within its territory. Upon death, it’s possible to extract a Chelis pherocore from its body.

rows.label: starfire
rows.desc: The Starfire mechanoid is a massive tank-like machine, equipped with a powerful cannon that fires very slow-moving unstable singularities. These singularities are generated by a complex fusion reactor at the heart of the machine, which channels and amplifies energy from nearby stars via microscopic skipgates. When fired, the singularities unleash devastating amounts of energy, capable of obliterating entire structures in a single blast, as well as creating secondary energy discharges that arc to nearby targets. The Starfire is heavily armored and equipped with advanced targeting systems, allowing it to rain destruction from afar. However, due to the intense energy requirements of the singularities, the Starfire is only deployed in the most extreme situations, where its destructive power is needed to turn the tide of battle.

rows.label: bantha cart
rows.desc:
Two banthas and a two-wheeled cart. Nothing on this world moves more weight for less trouble, and nothing looks less impressive doing it.

A bantha is a mountain of shaggy hide under a pair of spiral horns, and it is stupid in the specific way that makes an animal useful — it will lean into a load until the load moves or the harness breaks, and it does not form an opinion about which. They eat anything with roots, they carry their own water for days, and the Tuskens have built an entire way of living on them for good reason.

Use it for salvage: hull plate, machinery, whatever came out of a wreck too heavy to carry. It is slow, it is terrible off a road, and it will still be doing this long after the fast things have shaken themselves apart.

rows.label: thrumbear
rows.desc:
If you thought Thrumbos were tough and hit like a tank, may I present to you the answer to all your prayers. If you can feed the thing, this absolute unit would work extremely well as an assault force against any force foolish enough to threaten its feedstock. Plus you get to ride it on long journeys, possibly clearing entire forests on the way.

A colossal hybrid with recessive ursine genes. While proportionately it has a lower metabolism, its 50% increase in size still leaves it with a higher hunger rate than a thrumbo. They are however easier to train, hit much harder and can take even more punishment.

A general-purpose fighter plane, the Warbird is an incredibly fast and effective attack craft. With minimal cargo intended for holding maintenance equipment and fuel, its primary purpose is to engage other aircraft and initiate strafing manoeuvres.

Being a flying vehicle, it is extremely obvious when on the move.

rows.label: atispec
rows.desc:
Atispecs are strange semi-insectoid creatures that undergo a radical metamorphosis, similar to old terran butterflies. In their larval phase, atispecs are basically harmless: a medium-sized grub that feeds on plants and usually ends up as some predator's meal. Tens of thousands of atispec larvae hatch every season, and less than a dozen make it to their adult form.

An adult Atispec, however, is an entirely different matter: huge, carnivorous and venomous. Adult Atispecs are flying predators with a voracious appetite, and quite intelligent. There have been attempts to domesticate the adult specimens, but it has been found that it is not quite cost-effective to grow them during their 2-year-long vulnerable phase as larvae.

Art by Feroxiious (check her Instagram at https://www.instagram.com/feroxiious/). 

Based on a design by Brent Hollowell: https://www.artstation.com/brenthollowell

rows.label: Behemoth
rows.desc:
A Forsaken creature, which is believed to reside in the outer star belts. Legends speak of incredibly intelligent and fierce dragons, ruling over whole planets with their devastating fire breaths and incomprehensible power. The thunder is their voice and announces their coming. They were once hundreds, and are now but a few. On the last days of the Forsaken, they will rise again and darken the skies, when the day of judgement comes.

Special abilities: Behemoths were used as powerful beasts of burden by the Forsaken, and they can defend themselves quite well. Their flame attacks are quite dangerous. They can regenerate their wounds quite fast.

rows.label: thrumffalo
rows.desc:
One of the largest creatures in existence, dwarfing even the thrumbo and the mighty Gallatross. Capable of transporting a massive amount of material, producing a luxurious and excellent wool as well as thick, nutritious milk, they are almost the perfect farm animal. That is as long as you don’t look at your feed costs and die of a heart attack, but the scientists that designed this hybrid never had to worry about such things. Food is something for the proles to worry about.

A colossal hybrid with recessive muffalo genes. Completely herbivorous and with an appetite large enough to cause even large colonies to starve within a single season. This hybrid can prove worth the food costs as it produces thick, delicious milk every couple of days as well as luxurious wool every couple of seasons. Slightly more dimwitted than its progenitor and will attempt to wander off in search of food if not kept penned up.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> All colossal hybrids have very slow attacks, but hit very hard, and possess natural armor.

rows.label: mechathrumbo
rows.desc:
This hulking cybernetic behemoth is why you don't need tanks in the Rim. Its huge plasteel carapace hides a miniaturized synchrotron that constantly generates small amounts of antimatter, which is instantly used to fill a miniature antigrain warhead. Slow, but quite effective.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color>Mechanoid hybrids are always created with a controller booster, making the mechathrumbo effective mobile artillery. Mechanoid hybrids need very little food or rest, don't have psychic or toxic sensitivity, and have devastating ranged attacks. They have however high wildness, making them harder to keep tamed, and they will need a mechahybrid antenna to be built somewhere on the planet, or their IFF sensors will malfunction in 5 days. One antenna is needed for each five mech hybrids under the colony's control.

The Archocentipede is the end result of the Archotech Project, aiming to provide a "friendly" machine superintelligence with a capable body.
